summary: New sense 1b: (mit ʕal) zu einem Fest einladen
rationale: Specialised summoning to communal hospitality: the same host calls the surrounding Christians and prepares food for the seated guests. No new argument frame; retain as a subsense, with only one narrative witness.

summary: example for sense 1b in Infectum-wa (JTM 4.1/2)

data.turoyo: w mhawarwo ʕal u ʕulmo d kətwo hawir diḏe kule, yaʕni a mšiḥoye d kətwo hawir diḏe kulle mhawarwo aʕlayye.
data.translation: Er lud die Leute um ihn herum ein, d.h. alle Christen in seiner Umgebung lud er ein.

rationale: New invitation subsense and its ʕal-marked guests; both tokens quoted once.

summary: example for sense 1b in Preterit (JTM 4.1/3)

data.turoyo: aṯi u ʕeḏo mhawarle w səmle muklone, w u ʕulmo yatiwi axəlle.
data.translation: Das Fest kam, er lud ein und bereitete Speisen vor, und die Leute setzten sich und aßen.

rationale: New Preterit cell for invitation; meal supplies independent contextual support.

rationale: Fill Preterit sense 1 from three toward five; clear ʕal-marked addressee.

data.turoyo: mhawallale məlla heee tox larke tox.
data.translation: Sie rief ihn: Heh, komm her, komm!

rationale: Fifth Preterit sense 1 example; unusual suffixed addressee alongside feminine agent.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 5.3/46)

data.translation: Er sagte: Warte, ich will ihn rufen!

rationale: Unusual contracted 1sg Infectum; copy the supplied wording without expanding the form.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (61/327)

data.turoyo: An naʕime kə mhawrila li pire, kəmmi: “Ya pire! U sabʕano gdoxelax! Mə l aloho šqile minax? Arfiye!”
data.translation: Die Knabenschrien ihr zu: "Alte! Dieser Löwe wird dich fressen! Bist du verrücktgeworden? Laß ihn doch los!"

rationale: Unusual recipient suffix doubled by li pire, contrasting with the better-attested ʕal frame; preserves source spacing.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (JTM 5.1/10)
rationale: Thin Imperativ cell; unprefixed hawir and explicit called group.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 42/52)

data.turoyo: Marfele ad dalole lu paša bu Šam, omər: "Haweru bu Šam: "U ganowo ma d kətyo ṭro maḥwe ruḥe bu qrar d Alo, gdəbene mo kise w barṯi, ṭro maḥwe ruḥe."
data.translation: und schickte die Ausrufer in Damascus umher und befal ihnen: »Ruft aus in Damascus, der Dieb, wer auch immer er sei, soll sich selber angeben; bei Gott sei's gelobt, ich gebe ihm hundert Beutel und meine Tochter, er möge sich nur selber angeben«.

rationale: Thin Imperativ cell; plural Haweru and public proclamation differ from the existing singular call for help.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.16/797)

data.turoyo: ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Dalole kətwo. U ḥa d miḏayaʕwole mede, d əzzewole mede əzzewo mhawarwo baz zabəqone əmarwo: “Miḥasyo i emo w babo tərto səməqto mḏayʕo." U ḥa d ḥuzela d omər ‘kəlla!‘... Ya ste faro bə flan šəkəl. ʕEzo bə flan šəkəl ya flan mede hawi d mḏayəʕ kəzze kəmhawər aʕla.
data.translation: Uncle Isho: There were town criers. Someone who had lost something, something that had gone away from him, would go and call out in the streets and say: “May its mother and father be blessed, a red cow is lost.” Whoever has seen it should say, “It is here!”... Or else a sheep described in such and such a way. A goat described in such and such a way, or whatever thing may be lost, he goes and calls out about it.

rationale: II.1 Infectum-wa has one inherited example after round 1; habitual street announcement with quoted lost-property content is self-contained.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 2.4/866)

data.turoyo: Ǧan: Abuna, hani naqqa mhawriwo, mzaʕbəriwo ʕal nošo? Kətwolən qərbač, ya ste ġer mede b iḏayye?
data.translation: Jan: Father, did these shout, did they rage at anyone? Did they have a whip, or something else in their hands?

rationale: Thin II.1 Infectum-wa cell; plural shouting paired with threats and the addressee ʕal nošo.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 3.49/1378)

data.turoyo: Ǧan: Annaqqa lə mhawrituwo "aṯyo i Ġazale Barriye"?
data.translation: Jan: Then did you not used to shout, 'The Wild Gazelle has come'?

rationale: Thin II.1 Infectum-wa cell; second-person plural negative question with a quoted game cry.

summary: ʕal introduces the called person, including pronominal aʕle/aʕlayye; suffixed l-recipients also occur (JTM 5.2/21; 61/327). Distinguish postverbal l-marked callers in PrS 10/29, 16/58 and 20/28 from recipients.

Public sale cries, heraldic proclamations and battle cries remain within existing sense 1. The Kurdish derivation is already in the headword; these inflected tokens do not by themselves constitute a light-verb idiom.
Assimilated mhawalle/mhawalla contrasts with unassimilated mhawarle; contracted 1sg mhawanno occurs in JTM 5.3/46. No separate stem follows from spelling variants.
Infectum-wa includes habitual invitation (JTM 4.1/2) and unrealised past obligation (PrS 39/25). Repeated affirmative/negative calling in JTM 5.3/36 expresses ineffective effort in context.

Compact records lack verse evidence and cannot be independently checked. PrS 26/13 omits the shooting/roaring event from the supplied translation; no example quoted from it. Several old PrS citations appear to use another numbering system.

With ordinary calling, ʕal names an addressee; in lost-property proclamations it names the announcement topic (animal or missing item). This contextual difference should be documented without treating every ʕal complement as a recipient.
The Preterit and Infectum cells already have five and six examples after round 1. Jan's stale thin-cell proposals for these boxes are not imported.
Infectum-wa supports habitual announcements, repeated threatening shouts and a remembered game cry. The inherited example instead concerns an unrealized past obligation.
Mhawarli at Jan 2.10/2594 contains first-person -li; the reader's warning about machine-English participant tracking is justified. All added translations remain null.
Can the invitation subsense 1b be confirmed outside the single JTM 4.1 story?

Reconcile old prs 8/10 and 9/29 with the fox passage PrS 2/37; prs 40/31 with PrS 17/45; prs 105/24 with PrS 39/25; prs 114/10 with PrS 41/48. Do not replace these citations without the edition mapping.
Existing hwr.II.t.preterit.1 groups 25/71 under the fox quotation, but supplied 25/71 has Šaṭər Šuman shouting to the dead. Is 25/71 a further attestation rather than the quotation's source?
PrS 35/94 translation continues into unprovided verse 95; PrS 26/13 translation stops before the roaring event. Check source alignment before publication of those examples.
At 53/97, does the following komər introduce the son's response as the German indicates? Is Kəmḥawər an orthographic variant of hwr?
Check mhawir in w mhawir ḥarəwto yo at Jan 1.8/277. It may belong to the spatial hawir expression 'around' rather than an inflected hwr verb; no Detransitive box is accepted.
At Jan 1.50/2309 is mhawriwonne a call to people/animals or a misassigned technical agricultural operation? The listed sequence alone does not fix the referent.
Jan 2.10/2594: verify the speaker shift, retaining -li as first-person agent rather than following the machine-English pronoun.
Jan supplies no edition translations; provide verified aligned translations for the selected examples.
Animal callers and personified landscapes/stones retain vocal emission; natural rumbling of mountains is already covered by dröhnen. No participant-based new sense.

Town criers announcing lost property and public warnings corroborate round 1's treatment of proclamations within ordinary calling/shouting. Their profession does not establish a separate technical verb sense.
